spacr.qt.app.MainWindow.refresh_after_pr:
Redraw what a Preferences Apply changed, and nothing else.

THE APPLY THAT CHANGED ONE SLIDER REBUILT HOME. Page opacity is in
the window's signature, so moving it ran :meth:`refresh_theme` --
Home rebuilt (2.1-2.6 s on a loaded box), the tree retranslated
(0.3 s), every alpha gate walked -- while the only things on Home
that had taken the opacity were three rules, which
:meth:`HomePage.refresh_pane_surfaces` sets again in place.

:param changed: names from the window's signature whose values
    changed (:func:`spacr.qt.preferences._window_changes`).
:returns: ``"rebuilt"``, ``"in place"`` or ``"nothing"``, so a test
    can say which.
spacr.qt.preferences._refresh_owner_wind: Redraw the window for ``changes``, if it is still there.
spacr.qt.theme.finish_the_sliced_sheetin:
Pay every root still owed its sheet now. For tests and shutdown.

:returns: how many roots were sheeted.
spacr.qt.theme.sliced_sheeting_owed:
How many roots are still waiting for a sliced sheet.

:returns: the length of the queue.
spacr.qt.widgets.home.HomePage.refresh_p:
Give the masthead, the panels and the tabs the page opacity now set.

They took it when Home was built, and a new opacity used to rebuild
Home: 2.1-2.6 s of the GUI thread on a loaded box, for three kinds
of rule. Each is now set again in place, one widget per pass of the
event loop, and only where the rule changed, since setting a rule
restyles everything under it.

THE TABS ARE TOLD ON THEIR BAR. The tab widget's rule holds the
whole of Home under it, and setting it again restyled every tile
(1.1 s loaded) to change one tab's fill; the bar takes the selected
tab's fill as a rule of its own, which wins over the one it
inherits.

:returns: how many widgets will take a new rule.
Set one owed rule, then wait for the next pass.
